I built systems that ran call centers for a decade. Now I build systems that run themselves.
From Erlang-C to agents: I make complexity run on rails — 10,000 seats then, 24/7 AI stack now.

projects.name: Hand-built network & tailnet engineering (HERO)
evidence: LE DNS-01 over dead NS-delegation write-up
projects.card: A home network built by hand before 'agent' was a job title — tailnet, DNS rewrites, TLS over private domains, TCC forensics, self-healing services. The hero artifact: interactive topology proving builder-since-before-it-was-cool.

projects.name: The 24/7 Agent Stack (Mac Mini)
evidence: RAM table 34→8 processes / 10.3→4.8 GB (2026-09-07 real figures)
projects.card: A household AI stack that runs itself: multi-agent orchestration, 26 provider accounts across 14 services unified, self-healing services, live self-monitoring dashboard. Built to be boring — that's the point. Laptop node runs Omarchy (AI-first OS by DHH), customized with own shell plugins and packaged into setupclone. Toolbelt: evaluated Cursor/Open Claw/Cherry Studio/J.ai/DeepSeek Harness/ZCode — settled on herdr+omp. Choice by testing, not by hype.

projects.name: Chat·hector Demo — talk to the architecture
projects.card: Recruiters can ask the system itself how it works: a small public version of my household gateway with RAG over the entire architecture — natural-language Q&A, no personal data, soft token budgets, graceful quota.

projects.name: Docker homelab rebuild
evidence: OS/container updates in progress; media-automation framing only
projects.card: A self-hosted Docker farm on Fedora: media automation, monitoring, cron self-healing, Telegram bots. Docker, Linux, scripting, apps — different capabilities, same discipline. (Framing: media-automation engineering; no piracy references.)

projects.name: Chat·hector.app — private household AI gateway
projects.card: A private-by-design AI gateway for my family: Google OAuth SSO, custom model bridge (AgentRouter + Vertex fallback with JWT auto-refresh), Let's Encrypt TLS over a tailnet-only domain. Real users, daily use, zero data leaks. 'Counts only. Content never leaves the device.'

projects.name: Twitch Drops Watchdog
evidence: fully working; optimization + refactor in progress
projects.card: Reverse-engineered Twitch's drops graph — including a Kasada bot-mitigation token mint — into a self-updating public dashboard. The kind of system that breaks the moment the platform sneezes, and doesn't.

projects.name: This portfolio, built by its own system
projects.status: SHIPPING (v10 review, publish-ready pending green light)
evidence: every line passed the human gate
projects.card: A self-built four-model debate skill produced the starting line; an approval gate that only I can pass locked it in; and the site was verified with browser automation. A portfolio built by the systems it describes.
notes: v10 (2026-09-08): OG meta + favicon + og-card.png, career stats strip (10+ yrs / 10.000+ agents / 24/7 / 47 skills), closing CTA, print stylesheet, rebuilt stamp, a11y (reduced-motion + focus-visible), #method cross-link, tooling notes expandable, evidence lines refactored, flow diagram all-equal 2-line cards

DEPLOY.md + deploy.sh ready; gate: Mick green light

projects.name: Multi-provider LLM Gateway Engineering
evidence: write-up with numbers + honest reliability lessons
projects.card: 26 provider accounts across 14 services, 181 distinct models, unified in one config with per-model health verification — including the hard lessons: free-credit pools dry up, premium channels hammer down, WAF walls go up. Gateway engineering with the scars to prove it.

projects.name: The Job Pipeline (dogfooding)
projects.card: 23+ job sources, two scoring profiles, cross-board dedupe, delta digests delivered by cron to Telegram. Built it to find my own next role — it ships daily.

projects.name: Home Karaoke Pipeline
evidence: fully shipped, probed and working end-to-end (app + XLR mics + projector) 2026-09-07
projects.card: Reverse-engineered a 15-year-old karaoke download protocol, mapped the household's Spotify taste to it, wired XLR mics + projector + app. Proof that engineering is also a party trick.

projects.name: setupclone — portable agentic setup
projects.card: My entire agentic environment packaged as a de-personalized, replicable repo with one-paste installers. I don't just use agents — I productize my workflows.

projects.name: PVault — second brain on rails
projects.card: A knowledge system with a compile pass: inbox → layers → git-backed sync, per-device separation, integrity checks. The architecture is the product; the content stays private.

projects.name: 47-skill agent capability library
projects.card: A curated library of 47 reusable agent skills — from browser automation to protocol reverse-engineering to multi-model debate. Agents are only as good as their capability packs.

rules.evidence_rule: no card ships without a link, screenshot, or metric
rules.approval_gate: every publish passes Mick's gate after agent verification
rules.retire_rule: cards with stale evidence get demoted
rules.metrics: chat card: active-days streak, messages/week, uptime%, bridge requests, latency p50 — counts only
